premise: Readers can ask AI to write an initial implementation. These articles develop the decisions and evidence needed before accepting it.
scope: Second writing batch in PR 17. Superseded held status: the author requested publication after a more natural editorial revision. The October 31 release record covers this batch and the first batch; other approved calendars are unchanged.
research_method: Qualitative primary-source research and comparison with current site coverage. No keyword-volume, current Search Console, or private analytics data was accessed.
coverage_decisions: Keep the existing SQLite WAL writer and stale-snapshot article complete; add a distinct read-snapshot/checkpoint investigation.
Add actual HNSW plans and bounded scan behavior beyond the first batch's exact retrieval contract.
Rewrite the existing Claude Code CI guide at its current URL rather than create another introductory automation page.

articles.question: Why does a WAL checkpoint call succeed while a retained reader prevents completion?
articles.evidence: PASSIVE progress, blocked TRUNCATE, smaller threshold, released snapshot, final stored value and file length.

articles.kind: new article in the authorized October 31 release
articles.question: When approximate work remains incomplete, can an authorized exact fallback meet the required result count within its intended budget?
articles.evidence: Exact and analyzed HNSW plans, active scan settings, fixed predicate and corpus, limited and iterative counts, and five distinct authorized results from the completed serving path.

articles.question: Which code did the evidence check, and can a confident review bypass missing or unsuccessful verification?
articles.evidence: Synthetic positive and negative acceptance cases, source and requirement-harness identities, bounded proposal parsing, command construction without model execution.

sources.observation: Long read snapshots can limit checkpoint progress; existing site coverage emphasizes writer contention and sync behavior.
Checkpoint mode and all returned progress values matter; a successful call is not a complete application-level diagnosis.
Approximate candidates and post-index filtering can leave a result short; iterative scanning has its own limits.
An upstream report distinguishes plan selection from result completeness. Its timings are not used as predictions for this fixture.
Built-in tool selection, pre-approval, MCP denial, bare startup, turn limits, and structured output are separate controls.
The output envelope and presence of structured output must be inspected; command success cannot establish the application's review contract.

verification_policy: All compiler, build, test, and formatting checks run in the existing GitHub Content safety workflow with its configured runners. Article excerpts are checked against the compiled sources. Planned assertions become observations only after the corresponding run is inspected.
limits: Synthetic vectors do not measure real retrieval relevance or production performance.
The CI review fixture uses trusted-run stand-ins and makes no provider or GitHub API call.
No article or traffic target is inferred to outperform the others without equally aged site data.
